results.summary_before: TinyQV is a small RISC-V SoC implementing the RV32EC instruction set with Zcb and Zicond extensions, using QSPI flash for program storage and QSPI PSRAM for data memory. It includes a UART and an SPI controller intended for driving an ST7789 LCD, and is designed to work with a QSPI Pmod containing flash and RAM. Testing requires loading an image into flash and following a specific reset and clocking sequence, with MicroPython scripts on the RP2040 handling the setup. Silicon tests confirmed it runs CoreMark and MicroPython at 64 MHz with latency 1 or 2, and up to 100 MHz with latency 2.

results.summary_before: This prototype reads a 16-bit design ID from an I2C EEPROM and uses it to select the corresponding Tiny Tapeout project by driving control signals for the multiplexer. It also prints the read value over UART at 115200 baud for debugging. It requires an external 1 kbit or 2 kbit I2C EEPROM such as a 24C01 or 24C02 with 10k pull-up resistors on SCL and SDA. The design is intended for automatic project selection in Tiny Tapeout and is documented with specific expected behavior for the control outputs.
